title: a calibration candidate was silently discarded by the shared-family table
detail: candidate 'c_prob24' (disk_retained_peak 24000) produced a stream byte-identical to the registered one. Cause: Protocol023MultiRegimeBWGD2.regime_params overlays _REGISTERED_COMMON onto every regime, so writing the value only into REGIMES_V3[regime] left the family default (16000) in force. Fix: install_candidate now writes both tables and records the effective values in the candidate table.

title: the cascade probability override was silently reset by the phase switch
detail: a candidate with cascade_task_probability 0.45 produced a stream whose manifest declared 0.45 while every phase column carried 0.25. Cause: the collector's interval loop calls workload.set_active_regime(regime, probability=phase['cascade_task_probability']) at every switch, overwriting any probability set beforehand. Fix: a calibrated run rewrites the phase table itself (before the switch points and the manifest are derived), so the phase columns, the switch points and the manifest all carry the calibrated value.
detected_by: a calibrated development stream coming out with the registered prevalence and cascade-event count

title: the independent stream verifier re-checked calibrated streams against the registered numerics
detail: the verifier's phase-probability, switch-point and admissibility checks all read the registered tables, so a correctly calibrated stream failed them and a mis-generated one could have passed. Fix: --tag-suffix plus a declared-calibration reader that validates the amendment against the registered law (compute_first must not appear; sequence/onset_resource/response_windows may not move) and then evaluates the checks against the values the stream itself declares. Regression: all four round-1 streams still pass unchanged (61/61).
detected_by: the first calibrated dev stream failing 7 checks that were all traceable to the registered probability

title: the calibrated stream's null phases are no longer envelope-free
detail: raising the cascade probability leaves far more regime tasks in flight when the post-regime familiar phase starts, so the whole-familiar-phase admissibility scan measures 5200/5424/20000 instead of round 1's 1860/1400/9000. This is a real property of the calibrated environment, not a generator defect; the registered onset thresholds remain admissible against the genuine familiar window (phase F0, measured 1860/1400/9000, identical to round 1). Fix: the verifier re-measures admissibility on F0 and keeps the polluted reading next to it under polluted_window_reading.
detected_by: admissibility_measurement_matches_audit failing on the calibrated dev stream

title: familiar per-task extremes differ in the last float32 digit between the audit and the verifier
detail: the audit computes the familiar per-task maxima in-process while the verifier re-reads them from the float32 task_timeline; round 2A measured 5424.630666666667 vs 5424.630859375 (relative 3.6e-8), which round 1 never hit because its familiar maxima were round numbers. Fix: the audit comparison uses a 1e-3 absolute tolerance with the reason recorded; no other comparison was loosened.
detected_by: the calibrated dev stream's B admissibility audit comparison

title: fixed C does not beat the frozen baseline by the registered margin in any first-exposure regime
detail: late-100-interval PR-AUC gains of C over A are +0.0049 (compute), +0.0020 (memory), +0.0203 (io) against the registered +0.03; the whole-phase gains are smaller still (+0.0043, +0.0028, +0.0095). 0 of 3 regimes meet the margin, so directive 14's first step (C learns the current regime) is not satisfied and the forgetting step is not evaluated. The recurrence gate is also not attributable: C's relearning gaps (-0.100, -0.084, +0.154) are all SMALLER than the frozen baseline's own gaps (-0.084, -0.021, +0.212) on the same transitions, i.e. the gap is a property of the timeline rather than of C.

title: the mature gradient gate is admissible for the first time and reads STOP-GI
detail: with the residual bank matured by the S4 online run the degenerate groups are empty at all three checkpoints, so the round-1 INADMISSIBLE verdict is resolved. The registered rule then reads no conflict: mean cosines +0.71..+0.95 and negative-pair fractions 0.020..0.094, far from the <= -0.05 / >= 0.30 thresholds, at every checkpoint. This is a measured STOP-GI, not an inadmissible reading.
consequence: the gradient-interference justification for D is not supported in this scenario

title: the marginal-match targets are only partly met by the calibrated arms
detail: prevalence is now well matched (A 6.80%, B 5.45%, C 6.88%; spread 1.42 pp against the 4 pp ceiling) but event counts rose with the cascade probability (342 / 600 / 532, i.e. +75% and +56% against the 20% target) and the duration and peak-ratio targets are not met (B duration 0.346, B peak ratio 0.638, C peak ratio 0.315 against 0.25 / 0.30). The trade was deliberate: the event count is what produces the h=1 positives the directive requires, and the alternative candidates that kept the event count closer to A produced 2-22 positives instead of 51+.

title: the third specialist clears the reliability bar by one positive
detail: io-first reaches 31 within-regime positives at the registered 0.50 exposure/tail split, against the >= 30 requirement (the 0.30 split reading gives 44). Round 1 had 12. The margin is thin enough that this row should not be treated as robust without the confirmation seeds.
